title.narrative: Kenya Livestock Marketing & Resilience Project (Heifer Project International)
Kenya Livestock Marketing & Resilience Project (Heifer Project International)

description.narrative: Project main objective is strengthen the production and marketing systems for improved livelihoods and resilience among smallholder farmers in poultry and beef production in Kenya.
Projektets huvudmål är att stärka produktions- och marknadsföringssystemen för förbättrad försörjning och motståndskraft bland småbönder inom fjäderfä- och nötköttsproduktion i Kenya.

Sweden through the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) has signed a MSEK40 project with Heifer International Project Kenya targeting the livestock subsector. The four (4) years project is aimed at strengthening production and marketing systems for improved livelihoods and resilience among 38,000 poultry and beef producers (32,000 poultry and 6,000 beef and sheep producing households). The project geographical coverage spreads across nine (9) counties of: Kajiado, Isiolo, Busia, Kakamega, Nandi, Uasin Gishu, Trans-Nzoia, Nakuru, and Bungoma.
Heifer Kenya has set sights on delivering three pivotal outcomes, which are.
•Establishing resilient production systems for smallholder farmers, boosting their livelihoods. •Strengthening Market systems, Infrastructure, and fostering valuable business relationship between market actors; and •Empowering pastoralists, Agro-pastoralists, and Partner institutional capacities strengthened for Natural Resource Management (NRM) and conservation in all the project counties.

description.narrative:
Below we present some result from each of the Key Result Areas (KRA)
KRA 1 Production system established for improved resilience and livelihoods
Innovative Blended Extension Service Delivery
• Facilitated local actors to sustainably deliver bundled business and production extension services
• 15,599 smallholder farmers accessing advisory support.
• 14,029 farmers enrolled on digital platforms; 5,081 actively accessing digital extension via LMS.
Strengthened Poultry Feed Supply Chain
• Sustainable, functional demand aggregation model established for quality poultry feed.
• Partnerships with Unga Farm Care, Wonder Feeds, Pembe Feeds, and KAK Feeds improving feed access and reducing chick mortality.
• FOABs secured discounted feed agreements and flexible repayment terms, boosting resilience and business growth.
• 176 tonnes of poultry feed procured and sold to 13,019 farmers.
Sustainable & Functional Chick Supply Chain
• Established a sustainable day- and month-old chick supply chain linked to private sector actors.
• 10 FOABs connected with certified chick suppliers: Kukuchic Ltd, Kenchic Ltd, Uzima Chicken.
• Improved farmer access to quality, disease-resistant chicks, reducing mortality by 14.6% (from 34% baseline).
Production & Marketing Performance
• 93,576 certified day-old chicks (DOCs) ordered by brooders through private sector
• 62,173 month-old chicks (MOCs) marketed : fully vaccinated and of verified quality.
• 27,161 mature chickens and 751 trays of eggs marketed through FOABs.
Breed Diversification
• Transition from traditional indigenous breeds to high-performing dual-purpose improved breeds: (Rainbow Roosters, Kenbro, Kuroiler, SassoBroiler: Cobb 500, Arbour Acres, Hubbard Efficiency Plus)
Farmer Capacity Strengthening
• Enhanced skills in chick rearing, feeding, and vaccination through partnerships with veterinary associations, pharmaceutical firms, feed millers, hatcheries, and equipment suppliers. Improved technical and business capacities of ESPs and brooders.
KRA 2: Strengthened market systems, infrastructure and business relationships.
Strengthening Farmer-Owned Agribusinesses (FOABs)
• Implemented a 4-stage FOAB capacity growth framework to build governance, leadership, sustainability, and inclusion.
• FOABs advanced along the pathway e.g., Buco Youth, Kwanza, Sirisia, Ngaremara, Kakamega Poultry, Kakamega Ray, Ushindi improved governance, market access, and service delivery.
• Reto CBO, Ibanda Agribusiness, Kukubora, Ollessos transitioned from Stage 12, establishing business cases and systems.
• FOABs achieved net returns of USD 1,652, enhanced farmer loyalty, and expanded services (extension, feed access, gender/youth inclusion).
Sustainable Market Systems that respond to local and international markets
• Market activation & Trade facilitation: Behaviour change QBPM- aggregated goats (USD 11,216) for Genco Livestock Exporters
• Private sector linkages: Collaboration with Uzima Chicken & Kukuchic provided 93,576 DOCs to poultry FOABs.
• B2B linkages : 10 FOABs linked to Unga, Wonder, Pembe, Kak Feeds, boosting certified feed use from 82.5 154 tonnes.
• Financing: 16 FOABs 5 private firms adopted blended financing (Calf & Impact Funds); mobilized USD 78,097 in leverage funds, enhancing capital diversification and business sustainability.
KRA 3: Pastoralists, Agro-Pastoralists and Partner Institutional capacities strengthened for Natural Resources Management (NRM) and Conservation.
Rangelands Conservation & Resilience
• Improved Grazing Management: Enforcement of grazing plans restored vegetation, protected water sources, and boosted drought resilience for 345 pastoralists in Nasaru.
• Fodder Innovation: Groups like Olteyani improved feed access and inspired positive behavior change among Maasai in Kiserian.
• Land Rehabilitation: 280 ha restored (avg. 1.3 ha/household) showing strong resilience despite poor rains.
• Climate Advisory Partnership: Collaboration with Ignitia equipped 420 pastoralists with weather insights for smarter grazing and herd management.
KRA 4: Gender and Social Inclusion
• Empowered Decision-Making: Womens participation in household economic decisions improved significantly average score 2.77/4.
•GALS Adoption: 12 FOABs implementing GALS with clear visions and co-mentorship teams focusing on animal health, market access, and gender equality.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
